notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: reviewed_by is null, no hardware run and no ROS run was made. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper PythonObjectDriver is replaced by a direct Driver. The upstream JDS6600 takes typed pydantic SignalGeneratorConfig and SigGenChannel arguments and assembles framed ':w<fn>=<data>.' lines from parts, so a config-only PythonObjectDriver cannot construct those values and a SerialDriver/ScpiDriver command table cannot carry the runtime-assembled frame. The hardware factory in native.py converts the driver's plain channel values to the upstream typed config and enum; the fake implements the same public methods and G7 confirms them against the pinned class. The card lists two entry symbols; this package covers the second, hwtools.drivers.joyit.jds6600:JDS6600 (src/hwtools/drivers/joyit/jds6600.py:119). The DS1054Z scope entry is not covered: the package layout serves one device per package, so the scope needs a separate card. Mock path: the card's preferred upstream-sim is not usable as the G7 stand-in because SimulatedSignalGenerator implements the SignalGenerator interface, not the JDS6600 wire-protocol class, and the clone is never installed or imported by the gate. The package therefore ships an in-memory F0 fake, not a recording and not captured traffic; its start values are test data (1000 Hz, 1 Vpp, 0 V offset, 50 percent duty, SINE, both outputs off) and are marked # placeholder in fake.py. The fake was never validated against a live device. NOT COVERED: the arbitrary waveform sample array (60 slots of 2048 points at 12-bit codes) served upstream by upload_arbitrary/read_arbitrary; the scalar waveform, frequency, peak-to-peak amplitude, DC offset, duty, phase and output-enable controls are served. A channel that is already playing an arbitrary slot is not represented: its waveform reads as SINE (the upstream WaveShape default when arb_slot is set) and the slot is preserved by the read-modify-write path. The hardware backend (native.py, serial port discovery) was never imported or run; it requires a live JDS6600-15 and a deployment port. No site limits are needed because every numeric bound is stated by the clone. The last gate run passed all nine gates and reported no warnings.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Reviewed native.py, both card entry classes, JDS6600 acknowledgements, readbacks and limits against the pin. Changed driver.py to refuse frequencies that encode as zero before a native write, expose stored arbitrary-slot metadata and clear it on built-in selection, attempt both output disables after an exchange failure, and require explicit false readbacks; corrected fact ranges and clarified lower-bound citations. Changed fake.py to preserve arbitrary slots, enforce the tested model bounds and quantize phase; added failing-before-fix and missing-readback cases in test_driver.py. Updated facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; shortened tool descriptions to retain the 2048-byte limit. The final fake gate and strict collector pass with no warnings; this is contract_checked evidence only. For the human reviewer: The stop confirms output-enable register values, not the physical waveform; serial failure or an absent/true readback keeps it unconfirmed and latched. Up to six exchanges at the native factory default 1 s read timeout can exceed the endpoint stop budget, and upstream connect does not set a serial write timeout (jds6600.py:141-146). Shared-register read/modify/write is not isolated from other clients; disconnect itself does not disable outputs (148-151). Port discovery matches a generic CH340 VID/PID (105-115), so deployment must identify the intended JDS6600-15. DS1054Z was source-reviewed but is not served; arbitrary sample upload/download is also excluded. Apache-2.0 matches the card and no hardware backend or upstream code was run.
